documents.title: The decay-rate criterion: g must decay faster than e^{−x/2}
header: > The correct criterion is a **decay-rate** condition and I verified it numerically: the prime side Σ Λ(n)n^{−1/2}g(log n) converges for g(x) = e^{−x²/2} (partial sum 1.340983697 to n = 3·10⁵), converges slowly for g(x) = (1+x)^{−2} (9.784378427), diverges for g(x) = e^{−0.4x} (24.69442575 and rising, each term ~ n^{−0.9}) — so **g must decay faster than e^{−x/2}**, and a Gaussian qualifies. What actually obstructs truncation is **globality**: both sides are infinite and no truncation of either equals the other.
Round 5 restatement with the Gaussian transform:

> A Gaussian g(u) = e^{−u²/2R²} has ĝ(r) = R√(2π)e^{−R²r²/2}, which is entire and rapidly decaying in every strip; … The correct criterion is a decay-rate condition, which I then verified directly: the prime side Σ Λ(n)n^{−1/2}g(log n) converges for g = e^{−x²/2} (partial sum 1.340983697 at n = 3·10⁵), converges slowly for g = (1+x)^{−2} (9.784378427), and diverges for g = e^{−0.4x} (24.69442575 and rising, each term ~ n^{−0.9}) — so **g must decay faster than e^{−x/2}**, and a Gaussian qualifies comfortably.

documents.title: The envelope law: Σ_{n≤N} n^{−σ} sin(t log n) ≈ N^{1−σ}/|1−σ+it|
documents.source_line: ** [`research-journal.md`](../research-journal.md) — Round 3, "Measured: the rotation picture fails… Correction 1 — my exponent", line 288
header: **Source:** [`research-journal.md`](../research-journal.md) — Round 3, "Measured: the rotation picture fails… Correction 1 — my exponent", line 288

> *Correction 1 — my exponent.* I had claimed the envelope of Σ_{n≤N} n^{−σ}sin(t log n) grows like N^{1/2−σ}. **Wrong, and wrong by exactly ½.** By partial summation, with A(x) = Σ_{n≤x} n^{−σ−it}, one gets Σ_{n≤N} n^{−σ}sin(t log n) = Im[N^{1−σ+it}/(1−σ+it)] + O(log N), so the envelope grows like **N^{1−σ}/|1−σ+it|**. Measured envelope exponents (monotone envelope, N = 100 … 10⁵): **0.74995, 0.4985, 0.23223** for σ = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 — against predicted 1−σ = 0.75, 0.50, 0.25. Three significant figures, so the corrected law is confirmed. Consequence worth recording: on the critical line σ = ½ the envelope grows like **N^{1/4}** — which is precisely the exponent I originally and wrongly attributed to the *typical size* of the weighted partial sums.
- σ real, t real fixed; the summand is n^{−σ} sin(t log n); "envelope" means the monotone envelope over the oscillation.
